import re

def parse_duration(text: str) -> float:
    """
    Convert an ISO 8601 duration string (weeks or days with optional time) to seconds.
    Supported formats (uppercase only):
        - "P<n>W"
        - "P<n>D[T<n>H[n]M[n]S]"
    At least one component must be present.
    Numbers are non-negative integers, except the last written component may have a decimal fraction.
    Any other format (including years, months, lowercase, missing 'T' before time, etc.) raises ValueError.
    """
    # Regular expression for the allowed formats
    # Groups: weeks, days, time_part, hours, minutes, seconds
    pattern = re.compile(
        r'''
        ^P                                   # starts with 'P'
        (?:(?P<weeks>\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)W)?     # optional weeks
        (?:(?P<days>\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)D)?      # optional days
        (?:T                                 # optional time part
            (?:(?P<hours>\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)H)? # optional hours
            (?:(?P<minutes>\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)M)? # optional minutes
            (?:(?P<seconds>\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)S)? # optional seconds
        )?                                   # end of time part
        $                                     # end of string
        ''',
        re.VERBOSE
    )

    match = pattern.match(text)
    if not match:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid duration format: {text!r}")

    # Ensure at least one component is present
    if not any(match.group(name) for name in ('weeks', 'days', 'hours', 'minutes', 'seconds')):
        raise ValueError(f"No components found in duration: {text!r}")

    # Ensure 'T' is present if any time component is used
    # Since regex guarantees this, we don't need an extra check

    def _to_float(value: str) -> float:
        return float(value.replace(',', '.'))

    total_seconds = 0.0
    if match.group('weeks'):
        total_seconds += _to_float(match.group('weeks')) * 7 * 86400
    if match.group('days'):
        total_seconds += _to_float(match.group('days')) * 86400
    if match.group('hours'):
        total_seconds += _to_float(match.group('hours')) * 3600
    if match.group('minutes'):
        total_seconds += _to_float(match.group('minutes')) * 60
    if match.group('seconds'):
        total_seconds += _to_float(match.group('seconds'))

    return total_seconds
